answer: Each identity must complete a three-hour livestreamed painting session, mixing its own pigment on camera while the work stays as clear as crystal water in a lagoon, with random brush checks from a moderator every twenty minutes. A hired painter costs about $120 per fake, and the same hand or the same canvas twice is flagged and both identities are slashed. A farm of 100 fakes needs 100 painters and 100 canvases, so the price climbs with every fake added.
